main_text.p: enim animalia citius nutriri & augeri quibusdam animalibus arbitror. Porro id quoque deducit, omnes partes planta porosas esse, ob alimenti copiam, tenuitatem & calorem. Atque cap. 3. porositatis ejus indicium esse docet, quod planta in aqua supernatent: ejus enim causam esse, quia aer poris inclusus levitate sua prohibet descendum propter quam neque oleum, neque folia, neque lapides porosi, ut pumex, fundum petant: at ob carentiam illorum pororum ebenus nigra mergatur. Quae suo loco esse fi-no : attamen vide quae lib.3. c.7. de innatatione notavimus.
main_text.head: III. Augmentatio nihil habet difficultatis, quippe eadem ratione celebratur, hoc tantum differt, quod in ea plus appetitur, quam deperditum est.
main_text.p: IV. Generatio plantarum vel univoca, vel aequivoca est.

V. In generatione univoca quaedam nobis notanda sunt circa generans, varium productionis feminis ortum, primam partium omnium structuram, & earundem perfectionem, denique locum in quo proveniunt & confervantur.
VI. Circa generans quari folet, an sexus quoque in plantis sit? Ego non arbitror: attamen ejus quandam ἀναλογίαν non nego. §.1.

page.notes: Page is a running text page; the printed text was transcribed as set. Greek word "ἀναλογίαν" is a reconstruction of a partly worn Greek word ("ἀναλογίαν"); the first Greek word is uncertain. Word "porosas" for printed "porofae" and several words in the italic lines were read with [?] where doubtful; the line "omnes partes plantae porosae esse" is a reading of a worn line. The text at the top-right edge shows only a fragment of a neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
